scheme_name: Financial Assistance for encouraging production of Traditional Khell-Tiatr
description:
The Financial Assistance for Encouraging Production of Traditional Khell-Tiatr scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in 2021. 

This initiative aims to promote and preserve the cultural heritage of Khell-Tiatr, a traditional form of theatre that is an integral part of Goan culture. 

Khell-Tiatr is characterized by its unique blend of music, dance, and drama, often reflecting social issues and local folklore. 

The scheme was introduced to provide financial support to artists, playwrights, and production teams involved in Khell-Tiatr. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to encourage the production of Khell-Tiatr plays and to ensure that this art form does not fade away with time. 

The government aims to enhance the quality and quantity of Khell-Tiatr productions through this financial assistance. 

The scheme also seeks to create a sustainable environment for artists and performers by providing them with the necessary resources. 

The target beneficiaries of this scheme include local artists, theatre groups, and production houses that specialize in Khell-Tiatr. 

Under this scheme, the government provides a financial grant of up to ₹5 lakh for each approved production. 

This grant is intended to cover various expenses related to the production, including scriptwriting, set design, costumes, and marketing. 

The scheme also encourages collaboration among artists and promotes the involvement of youth in traditional theatre. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of Goa and being involved in the production of Khell-Tiatr. 

Artists must demonstrate their experience in the field of Khell-Tiatr to qualify for the financial assistance. 

The application process requires interested parties to submit a detailed project proposal outlining their production plans. 

This proposal must include information about the script, cast, crew, and budget estimates. 

Applicants are also required to provide a timeline for the production and details about the venue. 

The documents required for the application include proof of residency in Goa, identity proof, and any previous work samples related to Khell-Tiatr. 

The application must be submitted to the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The deadline for submitting applications is typically set for the end of each financial year, specifically March 31. 

Once the application is received, it undergoes a review process by a committee of experts in the field of performing arts. 

The committee evaluates the proposals based on creativity, feasibility, and cultural significance. 

Successful applicants are notified within a month of the submission deadline. 

Disbursement of funds occurs in two phases. 

The first phase involves an initial release of 50% of the total grant amount upon approval. 

The remaining 50% is released after the successful completion of the production and submission of a performance report. 

This report must detail the execution of the production, audience feedback, and financial expenditures. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of promoting Khell-Tiatr through various media channels. 

Beneficiaries are encouraged to document their productions and share them on social media platforms to reach a wider audience. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture also organizes workshops and training sessions to enhance the skills of Khell-Tiatr artists. 

These workshops focus on various aspects of theatre production, including acting, direction, and stage management. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹1 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022. 

This budget is expected to support at least 20 Khell-Tiatr productions annually. 

The scheme not only aims to preserve the art form but also to generate employment opportunities for local artists. 

By supporting Khell-Tiatr productions, the government hopes to attract tourism to Goa, thereby boosting the local economy. 

The scheme aligns with the broader cultural policies of the Government of Goa, which emphasize the promotion of local arts and heritage. 

The implementation of this scheme is overseen by the Directorate of Art and Culture, which is responsible for monitoring the progress of funded projects. 

The contact details for the Directorate of Art and Culture are as follows: 

Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa, Patto Plaza, Panaji, Goa - 403001. 

The official website of the Directorate provides additional resources and information about the scheme. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from the local community, with many artists expressing gratitude for the financial support. 

This initiative has also sparked interest among the younger generation to participate in Khell-Tiatr. 

The government encourages educational institutions to incorporate Khell-Tiatr into their cultural programs. 

This approach aims to instill a sense of pride and appreciation for the traditional art form among students. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort by the Government of Goa to revitalize traditional arts and crafts. 

By investing in Khell-Tiatr, the government aims to create a vibrant cultural landscape that reflects the rich heritage of Goa. 

The Financial Assistance for Encouraging Production of Traditional Khell-Tiatr scheme represents a significant step towards safeguarding the future of this unique art form. 

It highlights the importance of government support in preserving cultural identities and promoting local talent. 

The scheme is expected to evolve over time, with potential expansions to include more forms of traditional theatre and performing arts. 

Overall, the initiative serves as a model for other states in India to promote and preserve their own cultural heritage through similar financial assistance programs. 

The commitment of the Government of Goa to support Khell-Tiatr is a testament to the value placed on cultural diversity and artistic expression. 

This scheme not only provides financial assistance but also fosters a sense of community among artists and audiences alike. 

The ongoing support for Khell-Tiatr plays a crucial role in maintaining the cultural fabric of Goa for future generations.
